item.title: FDI increasingly innovation-savvy
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-15
FDI increasingly innovation-savvy Sophisticated supply chain networks encourage foreign investors to expand China's foreign investment landscape is undergoing a structural shift toward high-tech and innovation-driven industries as the country's industrial upgrading and growing demand for advanced technologies create new growth opportunities for multinational companies, economists and business executives said. The shift reflects China's efforts to foster higher-value industries, particularly artificial intelligence, intelligent manufacturing, biopharmaceuticals and green technologies, they said. Huo Jianguo, former president of the Chinese Academy of International Trade and Economic Cooperation, said China's technological innovation and increasingly sophisticated supply chain network are encouraging foreign investors to expand their presence in research and development, advanced manufacturing and emerging technology sectors. Huo said closer collaboration between foreign and domestic firms is also helping integrate global expertise with local market needs, thus supporting the development of more consumer-centric products and services. That view is in line with the latest data. Foreign direct investment in China's high-tech enterprises rose 35.1 percent year-on-year to 200.26 billion yuan ($29.92 billion) in the first eight months, accounting for 41.7 percent of the country's total incoming FDI, up 12.4 percentage points from a year earlier, said the Ministry of Commerce. Speaking at the launch ceremony of the China Development Report 2026 in Beijing in late September, Fan Gang, a prominent Chinese economist, said China's economic development has benefited not only from its comparative advantages, but also from its ability to attract and incorporate advanced technologies and management expertise through foreign investment and international exchanges. Fan said opening-up and foreign investment have helped Chinese industries move closer to the global technological frontier, enabling domestic firms to strengthen their innovation capabilities and gradually shift toward higher-value operations. Marshall Mills, senior resident representative in China of the International Monetary Fund, said China has made substantial progress in innovation, but further reforms and better designed policies could help translate tech breakthroughs into stronger productivity growth. Mills said more efficient capital allocation, stronger innovation incentives and further development of capital markets would help the country unlock additional growth potential and capitalize on more of the economic benefits generated by AI. Reflecting the growing role of China in foreign firms' innovation strategies, Germany's Freudenberg Group — which operates 30 plants and employs more than 7,000 people in China — has made the country a base for its humanoid robotics R&D efforts, opening a co-creation center in Shanghai in mid-September. Claus Moehlenkamp, Freudenberg's CEO, said China has evolved from a manufacturing powerhouse into an innovation-driven economy, giving the country a growing role in the firm's global innovation and production network. In humanoid robotics, Freudenberg plans to develop technologies and robot-related products in China — including sealing, lubrication and vibration-control components designed to improve robots' performance and service life span — for both the domestic and foreign markets, drawing on the country's fast-evolving robotics ecosystem, manufacturing capabilities and supply chains. Americhem Inc, a US producer of specialty plastic compounds and additives, put a new clean compounding facility into operation in Suzhou, Jiangsu province, late last month. The investment will enhance the company's capacity to serve customers in China and other Asia-Pacific markets. John Richard, CEO of Americhem, said this move will bring the company's technical expertise and production capabilities closer to customers in the Asia-Pacific region, particularly those in the healthcare sector. zhongnan@chinadaily.com.cn

item.title: China urges action on climate change
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-15
China urges action on climate change Scientific cooperation, environmental protection in the Arctic underscored China's former vice-foreign minister Fu Ying called for greater international cooperation on scientific research and environmental protection in the Arctic, saying climate change, rather than imagined security threats, is the real challenge facing the region. Fu was speaking during a discussion on Friday titled "How to Understand China", which was held as part of the Arctic Circle Assembly in Reykjavik, Iceland, the largest annual international meeting about the Arctic, which this year was attended by more than 2,500 participants from more than 70 countries and regions, including heads of state and government, business leaders, scientists, and indigenous group representatives. Delegates discussed issues related to understanding, protecting, developing, and governing the Arctic. Responding to so-called China threat narratives related to the Arctic, Fu said the real challenge currently facing the region is climate change, and that countries should devote more attention and resources to scientific research and environmental protection rather than engaging in geopolitical competition over imagined security threats. "Too much of today's geopolitical debate was built around imagined threats, which wastes valuable time and resources," she said. "Sea ice is melting, ice sheets are shrinking, and temperatures are rising. These are the real challenges that deserve attention." She called on countries to pool their strengths and resources, enhance scientific research cooperation, jointly assess the challenges posed by climate change, and make early preparations. Fu noted that a joint statement issued by the leaders of China and Iceland last year stressed stronger cooperation on climate change and green energy. Such practical cooperation can better demonstrate China's policies and intentions regarding its participation in Arctic affairs, she said. Speaking about China's development and its international role, Fu said: "China has no intention of seeking global hegemony, nor does it believe the world needs another hegemon. China has pursued peaceful development, rather than relying on foreign wars, military conquest, or the expansion of its sphere of influence." China is willing to strengthen cooperation with other countries and promote a more just and equitable global governance system, she said. Fu's comments followed a discussion organized by Tongji University earlier in the day, titled "China-US Relations in the Arctic: Prospects for Cooperation". Pragmatic view During that discussion, Pan Min, a professor and deputy director of the Center for Polar and Oceanic Studies at Tongji University, expressed her take on the prospects for relations between the two sides, based on their dealings in the Arctic region, which she said was a pragmatic view, rather than an optimistic one. "The Arctic should not be viewed solely as an arena for geopolitical rivalry," she told China Daily. "There are shared interests requiring international cooperation in areas such as climate change, scientific research, environmental protection, navigational safety, and emergency response. Cooperation does not preclude competition, nor do differences rule out collaboration … the key lies not in eliminating competition, but in preventing it from crowding out space for cooperation." China has long stressed the importance of people-to-people exchanges as a way to encourage communication and she said the world of polar studies is an ideal arena to promote it. "Interpersonal communication is crucial, especially given the current challenges facing China-US relations. Collaboration among scientists, scholars, and professionals can help both sides enhance understanding, reduce misconceptions, and build trust," she explained. "Even when the two governments hold differing views on certain issues, researchers can still cooperate on matters of shared concern, such as climate change, the marine environment, and polar science. Such exchanges not only advance specific projects but also create favorable conditions for higher-level dialogue. "International relations are shaped not only by state policies but also by interpersonal trust; sustained, open communication serves as a vital foundation for managing differences and fostering cooperation." Xinhua contributed to this story. julian@mail.chinadailyuk.com

item.title: From bouldering to BMX, emerging sports gain a grip
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-15
From bouldering to BMX, emerging sports gain a grip China's recent success in exciting new disciplines inspires a new generation As the National Day holiday drew to a close, young people took turns tackling a rock climbing wall at a gym in Xi'an, Shaanxi province. Some carefully tested each hold before moving upward, while others dropped back onto the mats and prepared to try again. For Zhao Yu'an, a young climber at the gym, the appeal lay in the challenge itself — figuring out how to complete a route and sharing the experience with friends. Earlier in the holiday, thousands of kilometers away, Chinese climbers had faced a very different test at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games. Zhang Yuetong won the women's bouldering gold medal, while Chu Shouhong claimed the men's speed climbing title with a time of 4.71 seconds. From street culture, climbing communities and grassroots training spaces to the Asian Games and Olympics, emerging sports such as skateboarding, sport climbing and breaking are reaching wider audiences in China. Major competitions have brought these disciplines greater visibility and helped establish clearer pathways for elite athletes. Their performances, in turn, inspire more young people to take up the sports.

item.title: Xi: Ensure stable supply chains
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-14
Xi: Ensure stable supply chains Fair: Business exchanges upgraded President Xi Jinping highlighted on Wednesday China's commitment to working with countries around the world to jointly uphold the multilateral trading system and ensure the stable and unimpeded operation of global industrial and supply chains. Xi made the remarks in a congratulatory letter sent to the 140th edition of the China Import and Export Fair, also known as the Canton Fair, which opened in Guangzhou, Guangdong province, on Wednesday. He commended the significant role of the Canton Fair in promoting trade exchanges between China and other countries since its establishment in 1957, saying that it has become an effective platform for China to expand high-standard opening-up and promote the building of an open world economy. Xi said that under the new circumstances, China is willing to join hands with other countries to expand mutually beneficial international economic and trade cooperation and advance universally beneficial and inclusive economic globalization, in order to inject fresh momentum into global development and prosperity. Co-hosted by the Ministry of Commerce and the People's Government of Guangdong Province, the fair runs through Nov 4, with more than 30,000 exhibitors and around 340,000 overseas buyers expected to attend. It features products ranging from consumer electronics and new-type energy storage products, to embodied intelligence products and smart medical equipment, with many cutting-edge Chinese-made products making their debuts at the event, according to the Ministry of Commerce. Premier Li Qiang attended the opening ceremony of the fair and delivered a keynote speech. He highlighted that an increasingly open China that is constantly innovating and honors its commitments will bring new opportunities, provide fresh momentum and inject certainty into the world. Noting that market connectivity is not a tool for rivalry, but rather an effective approach to creating incremental growth, Li stressed the country's commitment to promoting the continuous integration and mutual growth of its domestic market and the global market, and to building an open world economy. As a "super seller" and "super buyer", China is also committed to delivering more benefits to its neighbors and creating greater prosperity for all parties, he said. He expressed the nation's willingness to import more high-quality products, especially those with high added value, from other countries, encouraging more countries to lift restrictions and work with China to actively promote the balanced development of trade. While underscoring the importance of promoting mutually beneficial and win-win cooperation, Li said that China is always committed to promoting shared development. Li emphasized that China will continue to promote high-quality development, expand high-standard opening-up, and take active and pragmatic steps to add momentum to the world economy. The actions will include sharing more market opportunities with other countries, expanding more mutually beneficial cooperation and firmly safeguarding the international economic and trade order, he added. While further lowering market access thresholds to welcome more foreign enterprises to invest and thrive in the country, China will strengthen alignment of development strategies with other countries and support Chinese enterprises to invest overseas in an orderly manner, Li said. He also expressed the country's support for the reform and development of the World Trade Organization, and its willingness to work with all parties to explore future-oriented international economic and trade rules and promote universally beneficial and inclusive economic globalization. WTO Director-General Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala delivered a video address at the opening ceremony, saying that the remarkable development China has achieved offers valuable opportunities for the world. Noting that the Canton Fair is an important platform connecting China with the world, Okonjo-Iweala expressed the hope that all parties will work together to promote WTO reform and build an open, rules-based global trade system. Over the past seven decades, the Canton Fair has grown into China's largest and longest-running international trade fair, with the widest range of products, the largest number of buyers and the highest transaction volume. China's trade in goods rose 17.6 percent year-on-year to 34.78 trillion yuan ($5.2 trillion) in the first eight months of 2026, with exports up 14.6 percent and imports increasing 22 percent, according to statistics from the General Administration of Customs. Earlier on Wednesday, Li attended a symposium in Guangzhou, communicating with representatives of overseas buyers and exhibitors. He noted that in recent years, the enterprises participating in the Canton Fair have engaged in more diversified business exchanges. They are upgrading from mere trade partners to innovation partners that allow for better sharing of the dividends of technological progress, to investment partners that open up more space for incremental market growth, and to supply chain partners that can enhance the ability to prevent risks and withstand shocks, he said. The foreign representatives said that they are willing to cooperate with China for shared innovation and development.

item.title: New bridge linking China, DPRK to aid trade, exchanges
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-14
New bridge linking China, DPRK to aid trade, exchanges The New Yalu River Bridge connecting China with the Democratic People's Republic of Korea will officially open to traffic on Thursday, with a joint opening ceremony to be held by the two countries, the Foreign Ministry announced on Wednesday. The new bridge will further facilitate trade and people-to-people exchanges between the two countries, Foreign Ministry spokeswoman Mao Ning said at a regular news conference in Beijing. The China-DPRK Friendship Bridge, a one-way link built in 1937, was the only land route connecting Liaoning province with the North Pyongan province of the DPRK, according to Xinhua News Agency. A statement released by the Foreign Ministry said the two governments signed an agreement in February 2010 on the joint construction, management and maintenance of the border highway bridge. Construction of the 3,026-meter-long bridge began on Dec 31, 2010, with a total investment of 2.22 billion yuan ($331.69 million), fully funded by China, according to a 2014 Xinhua report. Located adjacent to the Guomenwan trade zone in Dandong, Liaoning, the new bridge is a modern dual carriage four-lane cross-border highway, which is expected to significantly increase port capacity, greatly reduce cross-border logistics time and lower transportation costs. The Dandong Port is China's largest land port and goods distribution center for trade with the DPRK. Data released by the General Administration of Customs in January showed that the bilateral trade volume between China and the DPRK reached $2.74 billion in 2025, a year-on-year increase of 25.5 percent. Data from Dandong Customs showed that the import volume of the Guomenwan trade zone exceeded 160 million yuan in 2025, with 22,000 person-visits participating in such trade during the year. "The opening of the new bridge fills a gap in China-DPRK land freight channels, significantly enhancing cross-border logistics capabilities, broadening bilateral goods circulation channels, and promoting the expansion and optimization of China-DPRK trade scale and structure," said Zhou Jingyan, deputy dean of the School of Economics at Liaodong University in Dandong. She added that the port in Dandong helps drive the aggregation of logistics, foreign trade processing and commercial services industries. "The new bridge will reduce logistics costs and shorten delivery times, directly benefiting numerous border trade merchants and local residents," she said. In the past, Dandong focused primarily on general trade, with most goods transiting through without local processing or industrial upgrade. Now, the area has developed a collaborative development pattern of border trade, general trade, and cross-border e-commerce, with the zone achieving dual-channel operation for imports and exports. "The new bridge opening will surely alleviate the traffic pressure on the old bridge and logistics will be more convenient," said Chen Quantong, chairman of Dandong Humaohui E-commerce Technology Industrial Park Co. According to Liaoning's 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-30), Dandong is positioned as a key node in domestic and international dual circulation, leveraging its unique location along the border, coast and river to become an important gateway to the Korean Peninsula and Northeast Asia.

item.title: Envoy: Xiamen ideal for BBNJ Secretariat
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-14
Envoy: Xiamen ideal for BBNJ Secretariat "The BBNJ Agreement requires a secretariat commensurate with its importance and promising future, and China's bid to host the secretariat in Xiamen would offer greater certainty and stability for global ocean governance," said Yi Xianliang, special envoy for BBNJ Secretariat Affairs of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, in an interview with China Daily. China nominated Xiamen in Fujian province on the eve of the agreement coming into force on Jan 17, 2026. The city joined two other bidders, Brussels and Valparaiso, which were nominated by Belgium and Chile respectively. The decision on the seat of the secretariat will be made at the first meeting of the Conference of the Parties to the Agreement in January 2027. Formally known as the Agreement under the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea on the Conservation and Sustainable Use of Marine Biological Diversity of Areas beyond National Jurisdiction, the BBNJ Agreement was adopted by consensus at the UN Headquarters in New York on June 19, 2023, after 19 years of negotiations. The agreement applies to the high seas and the international seabed area, which together account for two-thirds of global ocean coverage. It focuses on four areas: marine genetic resources; area-based management tools; environmental impact assessments; and capacity-building and the transfer of marine technology. Yi described the agreement's new regimes as an achievement in the development of the modern law of the sea, which would help to shape a fairer and more equitable international maritime order. It carries profound political significance at a time when multilateralism and the international rule of law face serious challenges, he said. China participated throughout the negotiations, contributing to a practical and balanced outcome, according to Yi. China signed the agreement on the first day it was opened for signature, and deposited the instrument of ratification with the UN secretary-general on Dec 15, 2025, becoming one of its first parties when it took effect. According to Yi, hosting the secretariat in China would advance the UN's ocean-related sustainable development goal. China's experience in protecting and restoring marine ecosystems and its capabilities in deep-sea and distant-ocean activities would also help to fulfill the agreement's dual objectives of the conservation and sustainable use of marine biodiversity. Yi also pointed to the geographical distribution of international institutions. Asia accounts for approximately 60 percent of the world's population, while most UN bodies and global treaty institutions are located in Europe and the Americas, he noted. Hosting the BBNJ Secretariat in China would help make global governance more balanced and inclusive, enabling Asia and the Global South to make greater contributions. City's uniqueness Turning to the choice of host city, Yi cited Xiamen's maritime heritage, environmental protection record, marine research capabilities and international cooperation as advantages. Xiamen, a nexus on the Maritime Silk Road and a "garden city on the sea", has 265 kilometers of coastline and more than 70 square kilometers of national nature reserves for rare marine species in its coastal waters, where Chinese white dolphins are frequently spotted, he said. The city's research strengths include nearly 5,000 marine researchers and 30 marine science and technology research platforms. It hosts the APEC Marine Sustainable Development Center and the China-ASEAN Maritime Cooperation Center. The Xiamen World Ocean Week has been held in the city for 20 consecutive years, with the cumulative number of participants from around the world exceeding 2 million, Yi noted. Following the launch of a direct service to London in early September, Xiamen has almost 30 international passenger air routes, he said, also citing its high-quality medical services, educational resources and relatively low living costs. On support for the secretariat, Yi said that China has prepared a fully equipped 15-story office building and two supporting buildings in Xiamen on a long-term, free-of-charge basis, which will allow the secretariat to move in immediately. To support the participation of representatives from developing countries in relevant meetings, China will contribute $3 million to the voluntary trust fund under the agreement. It will also contribute to the special fund to support capacity-building activities related to the agreement's implementation, he said. Yi also highlighted the bid's significance for the Global South, saying that it would help increase the representation and influence of developing countries in global ocean governance. "China is ready, Xiamen is ready," he said. "Choosing China means choosing a future of greater certainty and stability for global governance."

item.title: The tungsten mine helped power the Long March

The tungsten mine helped power the Long March Share - WeChat
Where did the funding for the Long March come from? The answer could be found in Yudu county, Jiangxi province. The former China Tungsten Mining Company was the first State-owned enterprise founded by the Communist Party of China. In the 1930s, tungsten ore was exported overseas in exchange for essential supplies, helping break through the economic blockade and support the Red Army's epic Long March. Tap to watch.

item.title: Huamao village turns Long March spirit into rural progress
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-14
Guizhou's Huamao village turns Long March spirit into practices of rural vitalization Huamao village in Zunyi, Guizhou province, was once poor and underdeveloped. Today, it is lush and thriving. In 1935, the Zunyi Meeting helped set the course for the Red Army's Long March. Today, the spirit of the Long March, combined with a practical, hardworking ethos, is helping write a new chapter in the village's rural vitalization. Villagers who have returned to their hometown have opened farmhouse restaurants, while traditional paper-making has been transformed into cultural and creative products. Huamao's annual per capita disposable income has risen from 12,600 yuan ($1,883) a decade ago to more than 29,600 yuan. Last year, the village received 710,000 visits, generating total tourism revenue of more than 24 million yuan. Times change, but the resolve to endure hardship and never give up remains. item.title: NEV share of new car sales hits new high in Sept
item.description:

NEV share of new car sales hits new high in Sept Share - WeChat
New energy vehicles accounted for a record 61.6 percent of China's monthly new car sales in September, data from the China Association of Automobile Manufacturers showed. In the first three quarters of 2026, NEV output and sales both rose by more than 10 percent year-on-year, while the cumulative share rose to 53.6 percent over the period.

item.title: Huining — From reunion to the roads of today
item.description:

In 1936, the three main forces of the Red Army reunited in Huining, marking the end of the Long March. Ninety years later, the mountains once crossed on foot are linked by highways, while rivers once forded are spanned by bridges. Step into Huining and see the roads that connect the past with the present. Copyright 1994 - .
